class.name: EnetHostedMeshTransport
class.brief_description: Mesh transport for [TickNetwork] between players over the internet, with a host that introduces and relays them.
class.description:
One node hosts the mesh ([method create_host]) and is player 1; it must be reachable on its port (a public address, or a port forwarded by the project). The other players join through it ([method create_player]) and get their id from it. The host introduces every pair of players: each player of the pair opens a socket, the host learns its public endpoint, and both punch through their NATs to connect directly. A pair that can't connect within [member punch_timeout] is relayed by the host. The engines see every player as connected either way; [method get_peer_path] tells how a player is reached. The sender of every packet comes from the connection, and the host assigns the ids: a player can't take another one's place. A relayed packet carries its origin, written by the host. The host is trusted: it assigns the ids, introduces the players and relays their packets. [b]Admission:[/b] a joining player first sends the join data passed to [method create_player] (a password or a token, for example). The host gives it to [member join_validator], which admits or refuses the player; nobody learns about a player, not even its id, until it's admitted. The players still joining count toward the limit of players, and an address can start a few joins at once, then one more every two seconds. [member SceneMultiplayer.auth_callback] only guards the [SceneMultiplayer] on [method get_multiplayer_peer]: the [TickNetwork] sees every admitted player, so check the players with [member join_validator]. The same mesh can carry [SceneMultiplayer] ([method get_multiplayer_peer]), so RPCs, spawners and synchronizers reach every player, relayed ones included. [codeblock] # On the host: var mesh := EnetHostedMeshTransport.create_host(9500) # On a player: var mesh := EnetHostedMeshTransport.create_player("203.0.113.7", 9500)
multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = mesh.get_multiplayer_peer() $Game.start(mesh) [/codeblock] [b]DTLS:[/b] pass [TLSOptions] to [method create_host] ([method TLSOptions.server]) and [method create_player] ([method TLSOptions.client], or [method TLSOptions.client_unsafe] for testing) to encrypt every link. The direct links between players use a certificate each player generates when it joins; the host hands it to the other player of the pair, who accepts only that certificate. A DTLS socket only takes DTLS, so the players register their endpoints on a second, plain port of the host (the rendezvous port, the next port by default), which must be reachable too; only single-use tokens go through it. [b]Host migration:[/b] the host keeps every player informed of a succession (players without relayed pairs first, then by id). When the host leaves with [method hand_over], or stops answering (see [member host_timeout]), the first player of the succession still in the mesh becomes the host: its direct links become the host links, and the others follow it through their direct link with it. A [TickNetwork] with [constant TickNetwork.AUTHORITY_SINGLE] moves its authority to the new host (see [signal TickNetwork.host_migrated]); [SceneMultiplayer] doesn't (see [signal TickMultiplayerPeer.host_migrated]). A player that can't reach the new host directly leaves the mesh. The new host has no listening port, so no new players can join after a migration. A host that stops answering may be gone, or only cut off from one player: before migrating, a player asks the players it reaches directly whether they lost the host too. If one of them still hears from it, or none of them answers, this player is the one cut off, and it leaves the mesh instead of taking over. A host that calls [method close] ends the mesh for everybody.

method.name: admit_player
method.description: Host: admits [param peer], a player whose join data arrived and that [member join_validator] left waiting. Returns [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if no such player is waiting.

method.name: close
method.description: Closes every connection. On the host, the mesh ends for every player; [method hand_over] leaves it to the next player of the succession instead.

method.name: create_host
method.description: Hosts a mesh on [param port] for up to [param max_players] players (the host included). The [param compression] mode must be the same on every node. With [param tls_options] ([method TLSOptions.server]), the mesh uses DTLS, and the pairs register on [param rendezvous_port] ([param port] + 1 when 0). Returns [code]null[/code] on failure.

method.name: create_player
method.description: Joins the mesh hosted at [param address]:[param port]; the id comes from the host, once it admits this player (see [method get_status]). [param join_data], up to 4096 bytes, goes to the host's [member join_validator]; it's only encrypted with DTLS. With [param tls_options] ([method TLSOptions.client] or [method TLSOptions.client_unsafe]), the host must use DTLS too; [param tls_hostname] is the name checked in the host's certificate ([param address] when empty). Joining with DTLS generates an RSA key for the player on a worker thread; the direct links this player accepts wait for it. Returns [code]null[/code] on failure.

method.name: get_host_peer
method.description: Returns the id of the node that hosts the mesh now: 1, or its successor after a migration.

method.name: get_multiplayer_peer
method.description: Returns a [TickMultiplayerPeer] on this mesh, always the same one. Assign it to [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer] to use RPCs next to the [TickNetwork].

method.name: get_peer_path
method.description: Returns how this node reaches [param peer].

method.name: get_peers
method.description: Returns the ids of the connected nodes.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns a [Dictionary] with [code]direct_pairs[/code] and [code]relayed_pairs[/code] (on a player, its links; on the host, the relayed pairs), [code]relayed_packets[/code] (host), [code]rejected_connections[/code], [code]failed_punches[/code] and [code]dropped_packets[/code] (received packets dropped because nothing consumed them: no [TickNetwork] running, or a [TickMultiplayerPeer] that isn't polled).

method.name: get_status
method.description: Returns the connection status. A player is [constant STATUS_CONNECTING] until the host admits it and gives it an id.

method.name: get_succession
method.description: Returns the order in which the players take over when the host leaves, as last sent by the host.

method.name: hand_over
method.description: Host: leaves the mesh, and the first player of the succession takes its place right away (on the players with [member host_migration] enabled). Returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] if this node isn't the connected host.

method.name: is_encrypted
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the mesh uses DTLS.

method.name: refuse_player
method.description: Host: refuses [param peer], a player waiting to join, and closes its connection. Returns [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if no such player is waiting.

members.member: When [code]false[/code], this player never tries direct links: every other player is relayed by the host. Set it before joining.
When [code]true[/code], a player takes the host's place when it leaves (see the class description); when [code]false[/code], the mesh ends with the host.

Seconds without an answer before a link is considered gone: a player's link with the host, the host's links with the players, and the direct links between players. A host that closes the mesh or hands it over is noticed right away.
Host: seconds a joining player has to send its join data and be admitted; then it's refused.

Host: decides who joins. Called as [code]validator(peer: int, join_data: PackedByteArray, address: String)[/code] once the player's join data arrives: [code]true[/code] admits the player, [code]false[/code] refuses it, and anything else leaves it waiting for [method admit_player] or [method refuse_player] (until [member join_timeout]). Without a validator, every player is admitted. [codeblock] mesh.join_validator = func(peer: int, join_data: PackedByteArray, address: String) -> bool: return join_data.get_string_from_utf8() == password [/codeblock]
Seconds to establish a direct link between two players before relaying them.
